note: ALL scenes are platform-original dialogue. Titles evoke classic Hollywood energy only — not licensed scripts from Casablanca, GWTW, Wayne films, etc.

scenes.title: Midnight Passport
scenes.premise: In a packed café at the edge of a closed border, an old love walks in asking for one impossible favour.
scenes.situation_before: Rick runs the café. Ilsa left him years ago without a word. Tonight she needs papers for someone else.
scenes.director_note: Subtext over volume. Let silences land. Think smoke and brass, not melodrama.

characters.name: Rick
characters.description: Café owner who pretends not to care.
characters.objective: Keep control without admitting he still loves her.
characters.obstacles: Pride; the risk of helping her.

characters.name: Ilsa
characters.description: Elegant, desperate, still dangerous to his heart.
characters.objective: Get the papers without destroying what remains of them.

dialogue.text: You still keep the same table free. Superstitious, or sentimental?
I keep it free so nobody sits where they don't belong.
I need letters of transit. Tonight. Before the last train.
You walk out of my life and walk back in like a menu special.
If I explain, you'll hate me. If I don't, you'll hate me more.
Try me. I'm in a generous mood — for once.
They're not for me. They're for a man who can still change the war.
And what am I supposed to change, Ilsa? The past?

scenes.title: After the Fire
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Southern estate · steel will · ruined fortune
scenes.premise: The house still stands, the money does not. She will not starve gracefully — and he knows it.
scenes.situation_before: Dawn after a disaster. Scarlett-like steel meets a practical man who wants her honesty.
scenes.director_note: She never begs. He never fully believes her softness. Play status like a duel.

characters.name: Cara
characters.description: Proud, strategic, refuses to be ruined.
characters.objective: Secure a path forward without looking weak.

characters.name: Clay
characters.description: Grounded, smitten, not stupid.
characters.objective: Get the truth before he offers help.

dialogue.text: You can stop smiling for the neighbours. There's no one left to impress.
There's always someone left to impress. That's how you survive.
Survive with what? Curtains and pride?
With whatever still burns. Pride included.
I can get seed. Labour. Credit. But not if you lie to me.
I never lie when the truth will buy me more.
Then tell me what you're afraid of.
Being ordinary. Being finished. Being someone who needs you.

scenes.title: Dust and Glory
scenes.premise: A quiet man with a badge won't leave town — and a young deputy wants to know why he stays to die for strangers.
scenes.situation_before: Noon heat. Word is out. The stage is coming and so is trouble.
scenes.director_note: Stillness is strength. Few words. Eyes do the work. Western-hero energy without parody.

characters.name: Cole
characters.description: Weathered, principled, slow to draw and slower to quit.
characters.objective: Hold the line without scaring the kid off.

characters.name: Jesse
characters.description: Eager, scared, trying to sound braver than he feels.
characters.objective: Get Cole to leave — or get permission to stand with him.

dialogue.text: They're six men. We've got two badges and one tired horse.
Then we don't waste bullets counting.
We could ride out. Nobody would call you a coward.
I would. That's the only jury I answer to.
I'm not ready to die for a street that never liked me.
Then don't die for the street. Stand for the kid behind it.
If I stay… you better not fall first.
Deal. You keep the sun out of my eyes — I'll keep the dark off your back.

scenes.title: Hat Check Heist
scenes.premise: A hat-check girl and a smooth grifter both claim the same stolen diamond is in the coat room.
scenes.situation_before: Charity gala. Sirens outside. One coat, two liars, zero time.
scenes.relationship: Rivals who might be perfect partners.
scenes.director_note: Speed. Overlap slightly. Win the argument, not the shouting match.

characters.name: Dolly
characters.description: Fast talker, faster hands, moral only when convenient.
characters.objective: Get the diamond and not get pinched.

characters.name: Nick
characters.description: Too handsome for honesty.
characters.objective: Beat her to the prize without falling for her.

dialogue.text: That's my coat. I can prove it — it still has my bad decisions in the pockets.
Funny. It also has my tip jar and your future arrest warrant.
Dolly, darling, crime is a partnership sport.
So is divorce. I prefer both solo.
Split fifty-fifty or we both leave in bracelets.
Sixty-forty. I have better shoes for running.
Fifty-five. And I buy breakfast if we live.
Deal. But if you call me darling again, I frame you myself.

scenes.title: Fog on Ninth
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Hardboiled noir · alley light · bad alibis
scenes.premise: A private eye corners the only witness who might clear him — or bury him.
scenes.situation_before: Rain. Neon. A body downtown and both of them look guilty.
scenes.director_note: Cigarette pacing without the cigarette. Short lines. Heavy pauses.

characters.name: Vance
characters.description: Broke detective with one clean suit.
characters.objective: Get her story before the cops get him.

characters.name: Lena
characters.description: Beautiful, careful, always one secret ahead.
characters.objective: Stay free without giving him everything.

dialogue.text: You left the club at eleven. The man hit the pavement at eleven-oh-five.
And you think my heels kept that schedule?
I think your fear did.
Fear is free in this city. Truth costs extra.
Name your price. I've got twenty bucks and a bad reputation.
I want protection. Real protection — not poetry.
Then talk. Who pushed him?
Someone who smiles like a saint and tips like a devil. Someone you already know.

scenes.title: Wrong Airport
scenes.premise: Two strangers argue over a boarding pass — then realise they're both running from the same wedding.
scenes.situation_before: Gate B12. One seat left. Two people who refuse to sit next to destiny.
scenes.director_note: Light and bright. Earn the soft turn in the last two lines.

characters.name: Amy
characters.description: Maid of honour who bolted mid-toast.
characters.objective: Get on the plane without explaining her life.

characters.name: Ben
characters.description: Best man who also fled.
characters.objective: Board first and not make a scene — failing already.

dialogue.text: That's my seat. 14C. I memorised it like a social security number.
Then your memory is as wrong as your tie.
This tie was chosen by a bridezilla committee. Show respect.
Wait. Are you escaping the Harrington wedding too?
If I say yes, do I still get 14C?
Only if you admit the shrimp cocktail was a war crime.
It was. Also the vows. Also my ex's new boyfriend's speech.
Fine. Share the armrest. If we survive takeoff, coffee's on me.

scenes.title: The Last Objection
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Courtroom · moral fire · one more chance
scenes.premise: A veteran attorney and a young associate fight over whether to put a dangerous truth on the record.
scenes.situation_before: Five minutes before the jury returns. The case can still turn — or explode.
scenes.director_note: Intellectual heat. No shouting until the final beat, if at all.

characters.name: Harper
characters.description: Young, brilliant, idealistic to a fault.
characters.objective: Force the truth out.

characters.name: Vale
characters.description: Seen too many pure cases die in pure ways.
characters.objective: Win without torching the client.

dialogue.text: If we don't put it on the record, we're not lawyers. We're cleaners.
Cleaners keep people free. Poets write about the ones who don't.
Our client is innocent. The file proves it.
The file also burns three other lives. Can you carry that?
I can carry honesty. I can't carry silence.
Then object. But when the room turns, don't look at me for shelter.
I stopped looking for shelter the day you hired me.
Good. Then stand up straight — and make it count.

scenes.title: Cable from Somewhere
scenes.premise: A soldier home on leave and the person who waited must decide if love can restart in twelve hours.
scenes.situation_before: Station platform. Train at dawn. Too much unsaid.
scenes.director_note: Gentle. Intimate volume. Let the last line breathe.

characters.name: Sam
characters.description: Changed by distance, still holding a photograph.
characters.objective: Learn if there's still a 'we'.

characters.name: Jo
characters.description: Kept the lights low and the letters stacked.
characters.objective: Protect their heart without closing the door.

dialogue.text: You look taller. Or maybe the world just got smaller.
I brought back every letter. Even the ones I never sent.
Why didn't you send them?
Because some nights I was afraid you'd stopped waiting — and I couldn't survive the proof.
I waited. I also lived. Both can be true.
Can we start from a new first date? Twelve hours, bad coffee, no uniforms.
Only if you promise not to disappear into a cable again without saying my name.
Your name was the only thing that got me home.

scenes.title: Docking Bay Blues
scenes.premise: A smuggler and a rebel courier haggle over the last freighter out before the blockade closes.
scenes.situation_before: Sirens in the upper docks. One ship. Two agendas.
scenes.director_note: Playful swagger. Adventure first, feelings second.

characters.name: Jax
characters.description: Pilot who sells loyalty by the hour.
characters.objective: Get paid and get clear.

characters.name: Rya
characters.description: Mission-first, trust-later.
characters.objective: Secure the ship for the cargo that matters.

dialogue.text: I need your freighter. Non-negotiable.
Everything's negotiable. Especially non-negotiable.
People will die if that crate stays on this rock.
People die if I don't get paid. I'm very democratic about tragedy.
Half now. Half when we clear the blockade.
And if we don't clear it?
Then you'll die rich in principle. I'll die useful.
Damn. I hate inspiring passengers. Ramp's open — try not to redecorate my ship.

scenes.title: Footlights and Fibs
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Backstage musical era · ego · big heart
scenes.premise: A temperamental star and a exhausted director fight over the finale — and accidentally fix their show.
scenes.situation_before: Opening night in ninety minutes. The finale is a disaster in sequins.
scenes.relationship: Creative enemies who need each other.
scenes.director_note: Big theatrical energy, then a sincere soft landing.

characters.name: Lola
characters.description: Voice of gold, patience of a gnat.
characters.objective: Keep the big note and her dignity.

characters.name: Max
characters.description: Sees the whole stage and none of his sleep.
characters.objective: Save the show without losing the star.

dialogue.text: I will not end the show in a trapdoor, Max. I am a headliner, not a magic trick.
It's not a trapdoor. It's a 'descent into wonder'. The posters already printed it.
Print a poster of me quitting. I'll sign it in glitter.
Lola — if you walk, the chorus walks. If the chorus walks, I walk into traffic.
Then give me the last light. Centre. No fog machine coughing on my vowels.
Centre light. Soft fog. And you actually look at the understudy like a human.
Fine. I'll look at her. Briefly. Kindly. Like a queen meeting a puppy.
That's the spirit. Now go warm up — and save my life with a high C.
